subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a config-only, rejectable Plugin SDK hook at the canonical pre-persistence boundary, and what trust, ordering, timeout, redaction, and recovery contract should govern it?
rationale: Existing validation prevents many malformed writes, but the requested mandatory external policy point changes plugin authority over persisted configuration and cannot be safely selected by an implementation worker.

options.title: Approve a scoped config policy hook
options.body: Define a config-only synchronous reject hook after built-in validation/preflight and before the canonical write, with an explicit Plugin SDK security contract.

options.title: Design a broader persistence policy first
options.body: Fold config into a general durable-write interception model so hook semantics are shared across config, state, and other persistent writes.

options.title: Keep validation built-in only
options.body: Decline third-party veto authority and continue relying on schema validation, preflight, tool allowlists, and external advisory tooling.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped config policy hook
recommendation.body: Define a config-only synchronous reject hook after built-in validation/preflight and before the canonical write, with an explicit Plugin SDK security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The recorded maintainer review already identified this as a config validation/mutation design-direction decision.
